points.description: States that TCP assigns a sequence number to every byte (or to each segment's data) so the receiver can order data and detect missing/duplicate bytes. Accept equivalent wording such as byte numbering or sequence numbering.

States that the receiver sends acknowledgements, specifically cumulative acknowledgements, to confirm which bytes have been received. Accept equivalent wording such as ACKs indicating the next expected byte.

States that the sender retransmits unacknowledged or lost data, naming timeout and/or three duplicate ACKs as the trigger. At least one retransmission trigger must be given; a bare statement that TCP retransmits without any trigger is not sufficient.
Mentions a checksum (or equivalent error-detection field) used to detect corrupted data.
Mentions the receive window (or advertised window) used for flow control.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all five ideas: sequence numbers, cumulative acknowledgements, retransmission with a named trigger, checksum-based corruption detection, and receive-window flow control. Each point is all or nothing; the two supporting details (checksum and receive window) are worth half a mark each. Vague claims that TCP is reliable or uses acknowledgements without the specific mechanisms earn no marks.
